Q: Which kind of task to implement to build a thread pool A:

You can of course use anything you like, but the point is the thread pool, so using a simple bit of code you can hand off to a thread and still get meaningful feedback that it is doing what is should is helpful. Do something that is independent of all other threads at first. Then consider having the task include a shared value or memory that is updated by the threads to exercise mutexes, etc..

In the past, in a similar exercise I would hand off a repeating timer with varying periods (e.g. 1Hz, 2Hz, 4Hz) from which the thread can do work each time the timer fires, anything from simply outputting the thread name and count, to adding to a shared counter later on.

The benefit is that a repeating timer process gives the threads something to manage that basically takes care of itself without requiring much CPU at all for learning with. The downside (or another benefit depending on how you look at it) is you have to spend a bit of additional time to research and write the repeating timer code (or whatever code you choose to run in the threads).

Don't use AI for learning projects. You lose the benefit of the deep understanding that comes from knowing the purpose for each character in every line of your code. Why it's used, how it contributes to the expression and ultimate function of your code? Vibe-code it and you end up with something you can hold up and say "Hey, look what the LLM did!", but not much learning otherwise.

Don't take this as knocking code-generating LLMs either. They have their place, but not much use in providing a deep understanding of how to write proper code.

Good luck with your project -- whatever you choose to feed the threads :)

Q: Small microsecond offset with recurent calls to gettimeofday A:

Potential Overflow

Consider what happens if .tv_sec is 32-bit.
The producttime->tv_sec * 1000000 is likely only 32-bit.

With tm = time->tv_sec * 1000000 + time->tv_usec;

Compare that to:

With tm = time->tv_sec * 1000000LL + time->tv_usec;
Product time->tv_sec * 1000000LL is at least 64-bit.

Q: How to use IF ELSE condition for SQL in Netezza A:

You could try and do this using case and dynamic SQL (you might need to check the syntax, since I haven't used Netezza much):

declare sql nvarchar(10000)
sql := case 
        when %input = 'Give' then 'statement1; statement2;'
        when %input = 'Take' then 'statement3; statement4;'
        else 'statement5; statement6;'
       end
execute immediate sql
